316	
317	    /// 30 Hz from the countdown's start, in `.common` modes (the type doc).
318	    /// Through `.countdown` and `.starting` it ONLY meters — the prepared
319	    /// session's level (#98 c; the recorder publishes nothing while
320	    /// arming, so the bar holds its last pre-roll level for that instant).
321	    /// While recording or paused: the microphone's level into the panel's
322	    /// own meter (`ScreenRecorder.publishMicrophoneLevel`, a no-op without
323	    /// a microphone and while paused, the recorder having silenced the
324	    /// bar), the elapsed time in the footnote and in the status item — with
325	    /// `paused`, which is what flips the item's menu — and a microphone
326	    /// problem into the note. `recordingDidStart` re-arms it.
327	    private func armTick() {
328	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
329	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1.0 / 30, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
330	            guard let self else {
331	                timer.invalidate()
332	                return
333	            }
334	            switch self.phase {
335	            case .countdown, .starting:
336	                self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
337	                return
338	            default:
339	                break
340	            }
341	            guard self.phase == .recording || self.phase == .paused || self.phase == .stopping
342	            else {
343	                timer.invalidate()
344	                return
345	            }
346	            self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
347	            self.refreshStatusLabel()
348	            self.statusItem?.update(elapsed: self.recorder.elapsed, paused: self.phase == .paused)
349	            self.syncMicrophoneNote()
350	        }
351	        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
352	        tickTimer = timer
353	    }

355	    /// The live note — what the panel says while a recording runs or is
356	    /// paused — rebuilt at every tick from its two PARTS and never from the
357	    /// label's text: `ScreenRecorder.microphoneProblem` the moment it is
358	    /// non-nil (a device unplugged, a writer that gave up), and
359	    /// `resumeProblem`, a resume the recorder refused (`+Pause.swift`,
360	    /// whose `liveNote` is the composition). Composing from the label was
361	    /// the R2 review's defect: a microphone did-finish landing late
362	    /// replaced a note that did not yet contain its sentence and wiped the
363	    /// resume's, and each retried resume appended its sentence again. Set
364	    /// only on a change, because `setNote` refits the window and this runs
365	    /// at 30 Hz.
366	    func syncMicrophoneNote() {
367	        let text = Self.liveNote(
368	            microphoneProblem: recorder.microphoneProblem, resumeProblem: resumeProblem)
369	        if noteLabel.stringValue != text { setNote(text) }
370	    }

372	    func disarmTick() {
373	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
374	        tickTimer = nil
375	    }

395	    static let inputMonitoringAskedKey = "FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked"

403	    var requestMicrophone: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void

407	    var requestCamera: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void
408	    /// Input Monitoring (CU-62), read only with Record shortcuts on.

447	/// recording) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s seventh file, cut out of
448	/// `+Recording.swift` when the press learned to open System Settings.
449	///
450	/// **The grants are asked for HERE and nowhere else, and UNCONDITIONALLY**
451	/// (decision 4: the TOOL never asks — it reads the status and refuses by
452	/// name — because a system prompt needs a person in front of it; the panel
453	/// asks, because a press of Record IS that person, exactly as the transcribe
454	/// sheet's Start is). **This is also the only place System Settings is
455	/// opened for them**, and the tool never opens it. Screen Recording is
456	/// asked with `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` on the FIRST press that finds
457	/// it absent — the system prompt appears once per app, not per launch — and
458	/// the ask is remembered in `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`; every later press
459	/// opens the Screen & System Audio Recording pane and the note says so.
460	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` returns false at once on a first ask, so
461	/// the refusal sentence is shown either way and the person presses Record
462	/// again once the grant is on. The flag is read and written only in a
463	/// launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks and never
464	/// remembers, because TCC attributes that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1).
465	/// The microphone is asked only when one is chosen, from `.notDetermined`,

470	/// deleted with the speech grant) — false for a scripted agent launch —
471	/// and the R1 review measured what that cost: under that flag the refusal
472	/// note told the person to press the button they had just pressed, and a

483	/// Screen Recording's table, remembered in `FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked`;

505	        let doors = Self.grantDoors

508	            granted: doors.screenGranted(), asked: doors.screenAsked(), launchedByLaunchd: owned)

518	        case .openPane:

539	        case .proceed:

551	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))

653	/// over the cap — the base file's toll, paid along the line the footnote
654	/// draws: its `.paused` and `.stopping` arms are what the pause added, and
655	/// `syncPhase` is its one caller besides the tick.
656	///
657	/// **Neither pause member is reachable from the panel's own controls** but
658	/// in a voice-over, whose panel stays up with a Pause / Resume button
659	/// (`+VoiceOver.swift`). The panel is off screen for every other recording
660	/// (decision 7), so Pause Recording
661	/// and Resume Recording are rows of the status item's menu, which calls
662	/// these through the closures `recordingDidStart` hands it, and File ▸
663	/// Pause/Resume Recording (`AppDelegate+Recording.swift`), the second door,
664	/// which calls them for the panel's own recording (#98). The panel's
665	/// phase — `.recording ⇄ .paused` — follows the recorder's own `pause()` /
666	/// `resume()` (`ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`), which are synchronous and
667	/// throw. The phase moves only AFTER the call returns
668	/// without throwing, so the panel never claims a state the recorder
669	/// refused: a pause that could not close the segment's file leaves the
670	/// recorder `.recording` and the panel with it, and a resume whose output
671	/// could not be added leaves both `.paused`.
672	///
673	/// **The two refusals are answered differently, on purpose.** A refused
674	/// pause BEEPS: the recorder is still recording, nothing was lost, and the
675	/// panel is hidden, so a note there would be read by nobody until the
676	/// landing, by which time it would be stale. A refused resume keeps the
677	/// recorder's sentence as `resumeProblem` and stays paused: the stream still
678	/// captures but no file is taking it, so what the person does next — try
679	/// again, or stop and land what was recorded — depends on the sentence, and
680	/// the landing's reveal (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`) brings the
681	/// panel back with that sentence in its note when they stop. The sentence
682	/// is STATE and never text read back off the label (R2 review): the live
683	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
684	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
685	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
686	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
687	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
688	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
689	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
690	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
691	/// to say.
692	///
693	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
694	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
695	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
696	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
697	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):

699	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold

704	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
705	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
706	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
707	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
708	    /// among them (the header).
709	    func pauseRecording() {
710	        guard phase == .recording else {
711	            NSSound.beep()
712	            return
713	        }
714	        do {
715	            try recorder.pause()
716	            phase = .paused
717	        } catch {
718	            NSSound.beep()
719	        }
720	    }

722	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
723	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
724	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
725	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
726	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
727	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
728	    func resumeRecording() {
729	        guard phase == .paused else {
730	            NSSound.beep()
731	            return
732	        }
733	        do {
734	            try recorder.resume()
735	            resumeProblem = nil
736	            phase = .recording
737	        } catch {

741	    }

743	    /// The live note's two parts, in order: the microphone's sentence, with
744	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone
745	    /// reads as a broken recording), then a refused resume's; empty with
746	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
747	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {
748	        var sentences: [String] = []
749	        if let microphoneProblem {
750	            sentences.append(
751	                "The microphone stopped: \(microphoneProblem) The picture is still recording.")
752	        }
753	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
754	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
755	    }

759	    /// The quit guard's call (`AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate`).

842	/// The recorder panel from the recording's END to the note that says where
843	/// it went (road map 3, R1c) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s fourth
844	/// file, cut out of `+Recording.swift` along the line `recordingEnded`
845	/// draws when the R1 review's fixes took that file past the 400-line cap:
846	/// everything before the session's `onFinish` fires stays there, everything
847	/// after it is here.
848	///
849	/// **One door for a finished recording.** The session's `onFinish` — called
850	/// exactly once whoever ended the recording: the panel's Stop, the status
851	/// item's, the system indicator's, a display that slept, a failure — arrives
852	/// at `recordingEnded`, which tears the recording chrome down (the tick, the
853	/// status item, and the `hiddenForRecording` flag that made `show()` beep —
854	/// clearing it, and showing NOTHING) and then lands. A DOCUMENT target
855	/// commits the placement through the document's
856	/// own door (`performGroupedEdit`, then `generateCaches`, the selection, and
857	/// the editor told through `viewStateDidChange`); a NEW PROJECT is
858	/// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, which does everything. A document
859	/// mid-drag is not committed over the gesture's base handle: the landing is
860	/// retried from a half-second timer until the drag ends, bounded at forty
861	/// tries — **20 s, kept** (lane C's flag, closed by reading): a landing that
862	/// waited for ever would hold the file's note back for ever, and the note
863	/// after the bound names the file, which is on disk either way — and on
864	/// either failure the note names the FILE, which is on disk whatever went
865	/// wrong after it. That timer stays in the DEFAULT run-loop mode on
866	/// purpose, unlike the countdown and the tick: a drag runs the loop in
867	/// tracking mode, so the retry fires when the drag ENDS, which is the
868	/// moment it is for.
869	///
870	/// **The commit is checked by its handle** (R1 review). `performGroupedEdit`
871	/// answers nothing: a refusal beeps or puts up the core's sentence on the
872	/// document's window and returns, and the panel — which cannot see either
873	/// — used to report "added" over a project with nothing in it. The
874	/// document's `project` handle changes ONLY on success (`applyEdit`'s three
875	/// outcomes), so `land` reads it before the commit and compares after, and
876	/// an unchanged handle is a failed landing with the file's path in the
877	/// note. The trial in `RecordingLanding.placement` sees everything the
878	/// commit will, so the arm is reached only by a race the trial cannot see —
879	/// an edit landing between the two on the same run-loop turn — and it is
880	/// there because the alternative is a note that lies.
881	///
882	/// **The note says six things, in order**, through `landingNote`, a pure
883	/// function so a probe can pin every combination without a landing: how the
884	/// recording ended when it was not this panel's own Stop (`.stopped` is the
885	/// status item's Stop too; `.userStopped` is the SYSTEM's indicator, and the
886	/// sentence names it so, now that Frame Job's own item is a menu-bar item as
887	/// well); that the document the person CHOSE had closed, when the choice
888	/// was a document and the landing opened a new project (R1 review — the
889	/// fallback is exact, and a person who chose "Untitled 2" should not have
890	/// to work out why a new window appeared instead); the segments left out
891	/// because their movie would not probe (`unreadableNote`, #97), each naming
892	/// the files it kept; the microphone's
893	/// problem, when the recording is a `.success` whose `micProblem` is set —
894	/// a success, not an error, so the picture lands first and the sentence
895	/// follows it; a resume the recorder refused (`resumeProblem`, STATE on the
896	/// panel and never text read back off the label — the R2 review's defect:
897	/// each end replaced the label whole, so after a refused resume and a clean
898	/// Stop the note was empty and the reveal showed nothing, the opposite of
899	/// what `+Pause.swift` promised); and the placement's own notes, one per
900	/// file the landing could not place. `failedToLand` names every file
901	/// through `filesClause` and carries the unreadable segments', the
902	/// microphone's and the resume's sentences too.
903	///
904	/// **The panel comes back ONLY with something to say** (decision 7, R2c).
905	/// It ordered out at `recordingDidStart` whatever the source, and each of
906	/// the three ends — `landed`, `failedToLand`, the failure arm of
907	/// `recordingEnded` — finishes with `revealIfNoted()`, AFTER its note is
908	/// set: the panel is ordered front when it was on screen as the recording
909	/// began (`showWhenLanded`) and the note is non-empty, and `showWhenLanded`
910	/// is cleared either way. A clean recording lands in its document or opens
911	/// its project and the panel stays away; ⌥⌘N shows it again. The reveal
912	/// belongs to the END and not to `recordingEnded`, because the deferred
913	/// landing's retries can put twenty seconds between the two, and a panel
914	/// shown with "Adding…" and no note yet is the dialog the user asked to be
915	/// rid of.
916	extension RecorderPanelController {
917	    static let landingRetryInterval: TimeInterval = 0.5
918	    static let landingRetryLimit = 40
919	    static let destinationClosedSentence =
920	        "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."
921	
922	    // MARK: - The end, and the landing
923	
924	    func recordingEnded(_ outcome: Result<RecordingResult, Error>) {
925	        disarmTick()
926	        statusItem?.remove()
927	        statusItem = nil
928	        launched = false
929	        hiddenForRecording = false
930	        switch outcome {
931	        case .failure(let error):
932	            phase = .idle
933	            setNote(
934	                [error.localizedDescription, resumeProblem].compactMap { $0 }
935	                    .joined(separator: " "))
936	            revealIfNoted()
937	        case .success(let result):
938	            phase = .landing
939	            landingAttempts = 0
940	            land(result)
941	        }
942	    }
943	
944	    func land(_ result: RecordingResult) {
945	        switch RecordingLanding.resolve(result.choice.destination) {
946	        case .document(let document):
947	            guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
948	                deferLanding(result)
949	                return
950	            }
951	            do {
952	                let placement = try RecordingLanding.placement(result, in: document, place: true)
953	                let before = document.project
954	                document.performGroupedEdit(RecordingLanding.actionName, placement.ops)
955	                // The handle changes only on success (the type doc).
956	                guard document.project !== before else {
957	                    failedToLand(
958	                        result,
959	                        ReelCoreError(
960	                            message: "the project refused the placement and nothing was added"))
961	                    return
962	                }
963	                document.generateCaches()
964	                // Every segment's clip, microphone clips included (R2b); a
965	                // segment that minted none is a nil entry, and its sentence
966	                // is in `placement.notes`.
967	                document.selection = Set(
968	                    (placement.clipIds + placement.micClipIds + placement.leftOutMicClipIds
969	                        + placement.cameraClipIds)
970	                        .compactMap { $0 })
971	                Self.editor(of: document)?.viewStateDidChange()
972	                landed(result, asNewProject: false, notes: placement.notes)
973	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: document)  // CO-81: its own step, first
974	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: document)  // AU-68: after the commit
975	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: document)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
976	            } catch {
977	                failedToLand(result, error)
978	            }
979	        case .newProject:
980	            do {
981	                let (opened, notes) = try ProjectDocument.untitled(around: result)
982	                landed(result, asNewProject: true, notes: notes)
983	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: opened)  // CO-81: its own step, first
984	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: opened)  // AU-68: after the commit
985	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: opened)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
986	            } catch {
987	                failedToLand(result, error)
988	            }
989	        }
990	    }
991	
992	    /// A drag is in progress: try again when it has had half a second to
993	    /// end, up to the limit — a landing over the gesture's base handle would
994	    /// be undone by the gesture's own end.
995	    private func deferLanding(_ result: RecordingResult) {
996	        landingAttempts += 1
997	        guard landingAttempts <= Self.landingRetryLimit else {
998	            let waited = Int(Double(Self.landingRetryLimit) * Self.landingRetryInterval)
999	            failedToLand(
1000	                result,
1001	                ReelCoreError(message: "A drag was still in progress after \(waited) s."))
1002	            return
1003	        }
1004	        landingTimer?.invalidate()
1005	        landingTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
1006	            withTimeInterval: Self.landingRetryInterval, repeats: false
1007	        ) { [weak self] _ in
1008	            self?.landingTimer = nil
1009	            self?.land(result)
1010	        }
1011	    }
1012	
1013	    /// Back to idle; the note is `landingNote`'s, over the placement's own
1014	    /// notes — the unreadable segments' sentences followed by what became of
1015	    /// their readable voices (#181 item 2), said only here, on a landing
1016	    /// that succeeded — led by every segment's camera sentences beside the
1017	    /// screen (`cameraSegmentsNote`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) — and the reveal
1018	    /// last.
1019	    private func landed(_ result: RecordingResult, asNewProject: Bool, notes placed: [String]) {
1020	        phase = .idle
1021	        rebuildDestinations()
1022	        // Then every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18).
1023	        let notes = [result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote].compactMap { $0 } + placed
1024	        let leftOut = [result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote].compactMap { $0 }
1025	        setNote(
1026	            Self.landingNote(
1027	                stoppedBy: result.stoppedBy, chosen: result.choice.destination,
1028	                landedAsNewProject: asNewProject, micProblem: result.micProblem,
1029	                resumeProblem: resumeProblem, notes: notes,
1030	                unreadable: leftOut.isEmpty ? nil : leftOut.joined(separator: " "),
1031	                camera: result.camera, cameraBeside: result.camera != nil && !result.isCamera))
1032	        revealIfNoted()
1033	    }
1034	
1035	    /// The files are on disk whatever went wrong after them, so the note
1036	    /// names every one (`filesClause`: each segment's movie, and the
1037	    /// microphone files that landed) — then what became of an unreadable
1038	    /// segment, the microphone, the camera (its `problem` and warm-up `note`,
1039	    /// spec §11 CAM-5, then each segment's camera sentences beside the
1040	    /// screen, CAM-10 (8)) and a refused resume, when the result or the panel
1041	    /// carries those sentences — and the reveal last.
1042	    private func failedToLand(_ result: RecordingResult, _ error: any Error) {
1043	        phase = .idle
1044	        var note =
1045	            "The recording was saved at \(result.filesClause) but could not be added: "
1046	            + error.localizedDescription
1047	        for sentence in [
1048	            result.unreadableNote, result.micProblem, result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
1049	            result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote, resumeProblem,
1050	        ].compactMap({ $0 })
1051	        {
1052	            note += " " + sentence
1053	        }
1054	        setNote(note)
1055	        revealIfNoted()
1056	    }
1057	
1058	    /// The panel back on screen after a landing, ONLY when it was on screen
1059	    /// as the recording began and the note has something in it (the type
1060	    /// doc). Called LAST by each of the three ends, after the note is set —
1061	    /// which is the whole point — and reached after the deferred landing's
1062	    /// retries as well, since nothing before it clears `showWhenLanded`.
1063	    /// Cleared either way, so a later `show()` of the person's own is not
1064	    /// mistaken for this one. Internal so a probe can drive both ways.
1065	    func revealIfNoted() {
1066	        if showWhenLanded, !noteLabel.stringValue.isEmpty { window?.orderFront(nil) }
1067	        showWhenLanded = false
1068	    }
1069	
1070	    /// The landing's note (the type doc): the stop's sentence unless the
1071	    /// stop was this panel's own; the closed-document sentence when a chosen
1072	    /// document was gone by the time the recording ended; the unreadable
1073	    /// segments' sentences; the microphone's problem; a refused resume's
1074	    /// sentence; then the placement's notes. Empty for the ordinary case, so
1075	    /// `setNote` hides the label. The R2 arguments, #97's `unreadable` and
1076	    /// CR1c's `camera` are LAST and default, so the probe's R1 rows read as
1077	    /// they did. A CAMERA result (spec §11 CAM-5) says its own stop — the
1078	    /// camera's `problem`, else that it stopped on its own — in place of the
1079	    /// display's, and its warm-up `note` follows the microphone's problem.
1080	    /// A camera BESIDE the screen (`cameraBeside`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) is
1081	    /// not the recording's stop: the display's sentence stays, and the
1082	    /// camera's `problem` follows the microphone's problem, before its note.

1135	/// at `recordingDidStart` whatever the source, and comes back only with
1136	/// something to say) — so this item is the recording's whole chrome, and it
1137	/// needs no grant and is reachable from every Space.

1139	/// It is created when a recording starts and removed the moment the
1140	/// recording ENDS — before the landing, not after it: once the recorder is
1141	/// finishing there is nothing left for it to do. The label is pushed by its
1142	/// owner's timer (`update(elapsed:paused:)` — the panel's at 30 Hz, the
1143	/// tool's at 1 Hz), so this class keeps no timer and no recorder; it holds
1144	/// three closures, `AudioNormalize`'s value-in-value-out posture applied to
1145	/// a control, so a probe can make one without the panel. It never asks
1146	/// whether a pause SUCCEEDED: the owner's next `update` says, by `paused`,

1148	///
1149	/// **The menu is rebuilt only when `paused` FLIPS, never per tick**, and
1150	/// the rows are replaced inside the one `NSMenu` the item was shown with
1151	/// rather than the menu swapped. A status item's menu may be OPEN when a
1152	/// tick fires — the tracking run loop delivers the timer (below) — and a
1153	/// title change under an open menu is harmless where rebuilding its rows
1154	/// thirty times a second is not; the flip itself cannot arrive under the
1155	/// open menu from the menu's own row, because a click closes the menu
1156	/// before its action runs. `menuTitles(paused:)` and
1157	/// `title(elapsed:paused:)` are PURE, which is how a probe pins both menus
1158	/// and both labels without a menu bar.

1161	/// owner's tick goes on calling `update` through its stopping phase, with
1162	/// `paused` read off a phase that is `.stopping` and no longer `.paused`,
1163	/// so a Stop from paused used to bring the coral dot back for the second or

5	/// The half of screen recording a probe can call: values in, values out, no
6	/// framework object that needs a bundle (road map 3, R1a). What a recording
7	/// IS before it starts — the choice, where its files go and the two
8	/// ScreenCaptureKit configurations built from that choice (the two grants
9	/// it stands on are `RecordingGrant.swift`'s) — so that
10	/// `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` can read every field back from a bare
11	/// Mach-O that never starts a stream.
12	///
13	/// `ScreenRecorder.swift` (with `+Pause.swift`, `+Microphone.swift`,
14	/// `+Finishing.swift`, `+Delegates.swift` and `+Content.swift`) is the other
15	/// half: the class that owns the `SCStream`, one `SCRecordingOutput` per
16	/// SEGMENT (R2: a pause removes one and a resume adds the next) and, when a
17	/// microphone is chosen, the `AVCaptureSession` for the second file. The
18	/// result types a recording ends as — `StopReason`, `RecordingSegment`,
19	/// `RecordingResult`, `RecorderError` — are `RecordingResult.swift`, moved
20	/// off the foot of this file at the 400-line cap; they are still values a
21	/// probe can make.
22	///
23	/// Three R0 facts shape the configuration and are restated on the fields
24	/// they decide (`archive/roadmap-3.md`, "R0 — the answers"):
25	///
26	/// - **The microphone is a second file** (q2). `captureMicrophone` on the
27	///   stream writes ONE stereo track that is the SUM of system and microphone
28	///   sound, which is decision 5's bad case — so `make` never sets it, and
29	///   `RecordingChoice.microphone` names an `AVCaptureDevice` for
30	///   `ScreenRecorder`'s capture session instead.
31	/// - **`.best` does not scale by itself** (q4). `captureResolution = .best`
32	///   at the display's point size writes a point-sized file; pixels come only
33	///   when `width`/`height` are asked for in pixels, so `make` multiplies the
34	///   point size by the display's backing scale under `.best` itself.
35	/// - **Show Clicks needs BGRA** (q6a). `SCStream.h` says `showMouseClicks`
36	///   "currently applies when pixelFormat is set to BGRA" and a fresh
37	///   configuration reads `420v`, so `make` sets `REDACTED`
38	///   when the stream draws clicks and leaves the default alone otherwise —
39	///   measured, a recording output over a BGRA stream starts and writes. The
40	///   stream draws the pointer and its click ring only In the picture
41	///   (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31): with Separate, `make`
42	///   sets neither and keeps `420v`, and Show Clicks lands the screen clips
43	///   with ripples instead (`RecordingLanding+Cursor.swift`).

213	    /// while a file of that name exists — the Finder's own collision rule.
214	    static func uniqueURL(in folder: URL, stem: String, ext: String) -> URL {
215	        let manager = FileManager.default
216	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension(ext)
217	        var counter = 2
218	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) {
219	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
220	                .appendingPathExtension(ext)
221	            counter += 1

244	/// The two ScreenCaptureKit configurations a choice becomes. PURE — every
245	/// field is set from the arguments and read back by the probe — which is
246	/// what lets the `excludesCurrentProcessAudio` mutant be caught at all: it
247	/// is invisible over MCP (nothing plays during a headless recording) and
248	/// this is the only row that sees it.
249	enum RecordingConfiguration {
250	    /// System audio is asked for at 48 kHz stereo, the rate the tap and
251	    /// `Loudness.swift` already assume of every file.
252	    static let sampleRate = 48_000
253	    static let channelCount = 2
254	
255	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
256	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
257	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
258	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
259	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
260	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
261	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
262	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
263	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
264	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
265	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
266	    static func make(
267	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
268	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
269	        let stream = SCStreamConfiguration()
270	        // R0 q4: pixels are asked for, `.best` does not scale by itself.
271	        let factor: CGFloat = choice.resolution == .best ? max(scale, 1) : 1
272	        stream.width = Int((displayPointSize.width * factor).rounded())
273	        stream.height = Int((displayPointSize.height * factor).rounded())
274	        stream.captureResolution = choice.resolution == .best ? .best : .nominal
275	        stream.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: CMTimeScale(max(choice.rate, 1)))
276	        // CU-31: the pointer and its ring are the stream's only In the picture.
277	        let inPicture = choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture
278	        stream.showsCursor = inPicture
279	        stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks && inPicture
280	        // R0 q6a: the click circle draws only under BGRA; the default `420v`
281	        // is left alone when the stream draws no clicks, so an ordinary
282	        // recording's pixel path is byte for byte the spike's.
283	        if choice.showClicks && inPicture { stream.pixelFormat = REDACTED }
284	        stream.capturesAudio = choice.systemAudio
285	        stream.sampleRate = sampleRate
286	        stream.channelCount = channelCount
287	        // ALWAYS: the timeline can play while a recording runs and must not
288	        // be in it. `captureMicrophone` is deliberately never touched (R0
289	        // q2 — the microphone is a second file), so it keeps its default of
290	        // false, which the probe reads back on every row.
291	        stream.excludesCurrentProcessAudio = true
292	
293	        let output = SCRecordingOutputConfiguration()
294	        output.outputURL = outputURL
295	        output.outputFileType = .mov
296	        // R0 q2: `availableVideoCodecTypes` is `[avc1, hvc1]` here and the
297	        // default is `avc1`; HEVC halves the file where the encoder offers it.
298	        output.videoCodecType =
299	            output.availableVideoCodecTypes.contains(.hevc) ? .hevc : .h264
300	        return (stream, output)
301	    }
302	}

389	/// "Enhance the microphone when it lands" (road map "audio" AP6 part 3, spec
390	/// §11 AU-68, AU-69): Enhance Voice run over a finished recording's VOICE
391	/// clips as a follow-up to the landing — never part of it. The landing commits
392	/// at once and is unchanged (`RecordingLanding`, `untitled(around:)`, the step
393	/// names, the notes); Enhance follows as its own undo step, "Enhance Voice",
394	/// once the voice's loudness and speech caches exist, because neither can
395	/// exist before the media is in a project.
396	///
397	/// The values and the pure decision are here: which files are the voice
398	/// (`voicePaths`), which clips they became (`voiceClips`), whether those are
399	/// measured (`isAnalysed`) and whether the document is in a state to take an
400	/// edit (`isBusy`), and `decide`. The two doors share them: the panel through
401	/// `follow` — a repeating timer per landing, in the run loop's DEFAULT mode
402	/// (the landing's retry trick: a drag runs the loop in tracking mode, so the
403	/// timer waits for it) — and `record_screen {enhance}` through
404	/// `AgentServer.landAndEnhance`, which polls `decide` from the server thread.
405	///
406	/// **The follow ends before anything is shown.** On any step but `.wait` the
407	/// timer is invalidated and the landing's pending entry removed FIRST, then
408	/// the step acts (`tick`): Cancel on the Measuring Sound sheet, no outcome or
409	/// a stale answer can never leave a timer that puts the sheet back up, and
410	/// `isPending` never depends on the sheet.
411	enum RecordingEnhance {
412	    /// One check every half second, the landing's own retry interval.
413	    static let checkInterval: TimeInterval = RecorderPanelController.landingRetryInterval
414	    /// Past this since the landing, a voice still unmeasured is given up on.
415	    static let waitLimit: TimeInterval = 300
416	
417	    static let notReadyHead =
418	        "Enhance Voice did not run on the recording: its microphone was not ready to measure "
419	        + "within 5 minutes."
420	    static let notReadySentence = notReadyHead + " Select its clip and choose Clip ▸ Enhance Voice."
421	    /// The tool's `.giveUp` sentence: the same head, a tool's way out.
422	    static let notReadyToolSentence = notReadyHead + " Call enhance_voice with its clips."
423	    static let noVoiceSentence =
424	        "No microphone clip landed on the timeline, so there was nothing to enhance."
425	    /// The panel box's tooltip (AU-69 (a)), naming AU-68's step.
426	    static let boxTooltip =
427	        "After the recording lands, run Clip ▸ Enhance Voice on the microphone's clip as its own "
428	        + "undo step, \"Enhance Voice\", once its sound has been analysed."
429	
430	    /// What one check decides (AU-68 (d)).
431	    enum Step: Equatable {
432	        case wait
433	        case enhance([UInt32])
434	        case drop
435	        case giveUp
436	    }

438	    // MARK: - The voice
439	
440	    /// The recording's voice files: each segment's microphone file, each
441	    /// left-out segment's readable microphone file, and for a voice-over each
442	    /// segment's own file — never the picture, the camera or the system audio.
443	    /// None without a microphone. Pure; empty paths dropped, each path once.
444	    static func voicePaths(of result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
445	        guard result.choice.microphone != nil else { return [] }
446	        var paths = result.segments.compactMap { $0.micDescriptor?.path }
447	        paths += result.unreadable.compactMap { $0.micDescriptor?.path }
448	        if result.isVoiceOver { paths += result.segments.map { $0.descriptor.path } }
449	        var seen: Set<String> = []
450	        return paths.filter { !$0.isEmpty && seen.insert($0).inserted }
451	    }
452	
453	    /// Every clip in the open container whose media is one of the voice
454	    /// files, in clip-id order. Main, after the landing's commit.
455	    static func voiceClips(of result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
456	        let paths = Set(voicePaths(of: result))
457	        guard !paths.isEmpty else { return [] }
458	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
459	        return snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
460	            snapshot.media(for: clip).map { paths.contains($0.path) } ?? false
461	        }.map(\.id).sorted()
462	    }
463	
464	    /// The clips still in the open container. Main.
465	    static func present(_ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
466	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
467	        return clips.filter { snapshot.clip($0) != nil }
468	    }
469	
470	    /// Each clip's media has a current loudness cache, and its speech saved,
471	    /// or a current speech cache, or no speech model at all (AU-68 (b)). False
472	    /// for no clips, a missing file or no cache folder. Main.
473	    static func isAnalysed(_ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument) -> Bool {
474	        guard !clips.isEmpty, let cacheDir = document.cacheDirectory else { return false }
475	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
476	        for id in clips {
477	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id), let media = snapshot.media(for: clip),
478	                let url = mediaURL(for: media)
479	            else { return false }
480	            let stamp = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: media, url: url)
481	            guard MediaImporter.loudnessIsCurrent(for: media, stamp: stamp, in: cacheDir) else {
482	                return false
483	            }
484	            guard media.speech != nil
485	                || MediaImporter.speechIsCurrent(for: media, stamp: stamp, in: cacheDir)
486	                || !SileroVAD.isAvailable
487	            else { return false }
488	        }
489	        return true
490	    }
491	
492	    /// A drag in progress, or the open container is not the landing's. The
493	    /// panel adds its own window test in `tick`. Main.
494	    static func isBusy(_ document: ProjectDocument, scope: UInt32?) -> Bool {
495	        document.isLiveEditing || document.scope != scope
496	    }
497	
498	    /// AU-68 (d), in this order. Pure.
499	    static func decide(clips: [UInt32], analysed: Bool, busy: Bool, elapsed: TimeInterval) -> Step {
500	        if clips.isEmpty { return .drop }
501	        if analysed && !busy { return .enhance(clips) }
502	        if elapsed >= waitLimit { return .giveUp }
503	        return .wait
504	    }

506	    // MARK: - The panel's follow
507	
508	    /// One landing's follow: its document, its clips, the scope it landed in,
509	    /// when, and the timer.
510	    private final class Follow {
511	        weak var document: ProjectDocument?
512	        var clips: [UInt32]
513	        var scope: UInt32?
514	        var started: Date
515	        var timer: Timer?
516	
517	        init(document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32], scope: UInt32?) {
518	            self.document = document
519	            self.clips = clips
520	            self.scope = scope
521	            self.started = Date()
522	        }
523	    }
524	
525	    /// The follows under way, by the document's `recipeKey` (never minted
526	    /// twice). A second landing into a document with a follow under way joins
527	    /// it: its clips are added and the clock and scope start again.
528	    private static var follows: [Int: Follow] = [:]
529	
530	    /// The panel's landing hands its result here once it has committed. A
531	    /// no-op unless the choice asked for it. Main.
532	    static func follow(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument) {
533	        guard result.choice.enhanceMicrophone else { return }
534	        let clips = voiceClips(of: result, in: document)
535	        let key = document.recipeKey
536	        if let pending = follows[key] {
537	            pending.clips = Array(Set(pending.clips + clips)).sorted()
538	            pending.scope = document.scope
539	            pending.started = Date()
540	            return
541	        }
542	        let follow = Follow(document: document, clips: clips, scope: document.scope)
543	        follows[key] = follow
544	        // `scheduledTimer` adds it in the DEFAULT mode: it waits out a drag.
545	        follow.timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: checkInterval, repeats: true) {
546	            [weak document] timer in
547	            guard let document else {
548	                timer.invalidate()
549	                follows[key] = nil
550	                return
551	            }
552	            tick(document)
553	        }
554	    }
555	
556	    /// True only while a follow's timer runs for `document`. Main.
557	    static func isPending(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> Bool {
558	        follows[document.recipeKey] != nil
559	    }
560	
561	    /// The timer of `document`'s follow, nil with none — what the probe reads
562	    /// back after a step (P5). Main.
563	    static func timer(of document: ProjectDocument) -> Timer? {
564	        follows[document.recipeKey]?.timer
565	    }
566	
567	    /// One firing: decide, and on any step but `.wait` end the follow FIRST
568	    /// (the type doc), then act. Main.
569	    static func tick(_ document: ProjectDocument) {
570	        guard let follow = follows[document.recipeKey] else { return }
571	        let clips = present(follow.clips, in: document)
572	        let window = RecorderPanelController.editor(of: document)?.view.window
573	        let busy =
574	            isBusy(document, scope: follow.scope) || window == nil || window?.attachedSheet != nil
575	        let step = decide(
576	            clips: clips, analysed: isAnalysed(clips, in: document), busy: busy,
577	            elapsed: Date().timeIntervalSince(follow.started))
578	        guard step != .wait else { return }
579	        end(follow, key: document.recipeKey)
580	        switch step {
581	        case .enhance(let ids):
582	            guard let window else { return refuse(notReadySentence, in: document) }
583	            AudioMeasureDoor.enhanceLanded(document: document, clips: ids, window: window)
584	        case .giveUp:
585	            refuse(notReadySentence, in: document)
586	        case .drop, .wait:
587	            break
588	        }
589	    }
590	
591	    private static func end(_ follow: Follow, key: Int) {
592	        follow.timer?.invalidate()
593	        follows[key] = nil
594	    }

596	    /// A refusal of `enhance_voice` at the inspector's foot; no beep (AU-68 (e)).
597	    static func refuse(_ reason: String, in document: ProjectDocument) {
598	        NotificationCenter.default.post(
599	            name: .projectDocumentDidRefuse, object: document,
600	            userInfo: [
601	                "refusal": ReelRefusal(op: AudioMeasureDoor.Command.enhanceVoice.tool, reason: reason)
602	            ])
603	    }

620	/// the server thread.
621	enum RecordingPolish {
622	    /// The three commands, in the order they run.
623	    enum Command: String, CaseIterable {
624	        case autoZoom = "auto_zoom"
625	        case shortcutOverlays = "shortcut_overlays"
626	        case speedUpTyping = "speed_up_typing"
627	
628	        /// Each command's undo step, its `actionName`.
629	        var title: String {
630	            switch self {
631	            case .autoZoom: return AutoZoom.actionName
632	            case .shortcutOverlays: return ShortcutOverlays.actionName
633	            case .speedUpTyping: return SpeedUpTyping.actionName
634	            }
635	        }
636

638	        var menuPath: String {
639	            switch self {
640	            case .autoZoom: return "Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…"
641	            case .shortcutOverlays: return "Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays"
642	            case .speedUpTyping: return "Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…"
643	            }
644	        }
645	    }

647	    /// What one check decides (CU-101 (e)).
648	    enum Step: Equatable {
649	        case wait
650	        case run(Command, [UInt32])
651	        case drop
652	        case giveUp(Command)
653	    }

655	    /// One check every half second, the landing's (and Enhance's) own interval.
656	    static let checkInterval: TimeInterval = RecordingEnhance.checkInterval

658	    static let waitLimit: TimeInterval = 300

660	    /// The commands `choice` asks for, always in `allCases` order.
661	    static func commands(of choice: RecordingChoice) -> [Command] {
662	        Command.allCases.filter { command in
663	            switch command {
664	            case .autoZoom: return choice.autoZoom
665	            case .shortcutOverlays: return choice.shortcutOverlays
666	            case .speedUpTyping: return choice.speedUpTyping

674	    /// segments are no screen. Pure; empty paths dropped, each path once.

714	                clips.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }, tracks: tracks,
715	                project: document.editedProject, cacheDirectory: document.cacheDirectory,
716	                settings: speedUp, from: nil, to: nil)
717	        } catch {
718	            return true
719	        }
720	        guard case .waiting = outcome else {
721	            cachesStarted.remove(document.recipeKey)

723	        }
724	        if cachesStarted.insert(document.recipeKey).inserted { document.generateCaches() }

800	    static func cameraClips(_ paths: [String], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
801	        let wanted = Set(paths)

803	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
804	        return snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
805	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip), wanted.contains(media.path) else {

813	    /// Background writes. Pure over the ids.

815	        clips.map { .setVideo(clips: [$0], patch: VideoPatch(cutout: .some(CutoutProps()))) }

818	    /// When the recording's choice asks for it, its camera clips cut out as ONE grouped step
819	    /// "Remove Background" (`performGroupedEdit`: a landing is not an AppKit event). Answers the
820	    /// clips the step was asked for, empty when the choice did not ask or no camera clip
821	    /// qualifies (the panel is then quiet; the tool answers `noCameraSentence`). Main.
822	    @discardableResult static func apply(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument)
823	        -> [UInt32]

861	/// granted the wrong application and be refused again with no way to tell
862	/// why. The pane sentence stays the PREFIX — `recording_proof.py` matches
863	/// on it — and the clause names the launching process's pid.
864	enum RecordingGrant {
865	    /// `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()` — true when this PROCESS may

883	    /// follows for a process launched from a shell.

1032	/// File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) and the welcome window's third button —
1033	/// road map 3, R1c. Two `@objc` actions and nothing stored, on purpose:
1034	/// `AppDelegate` has no stored properties, and the chrome probes
1035	/// (`phase6_chrome.py`, `phase9_probe.py`) instantiate `AppDelegate()` to
1036	/// build the menu bar, so anything stored here would be built in every one
1037	/// of them. The panel is `RecorderPanelController.shared` — one instance for
1038	/// the life of the process, `ExportQueueWindowController`'s mould — because it
1039	/// outlives documents and must exist with none open, and the recorder is
1040	/// `ScreenRecorder.shared`.
1041	///
1042	/// It is a nil-target action, `newProject`'s shape (`AppDelegate.swift`): the
1043	/// item resolves down the responder chain to the application delegate, which
1044	/// is what lets it work from the welcome window and from a document window
1045	/// alike. While a recording runs — PAUSED included: `isRecording` is every
1046	/// state past idle — the same item reads "Stop Recording"
1047	/// (`AppDelegate.validateMenuItem` retitles it from `ScreenRecorder.shared`),
1048	/// and this action then stops instead of showing. File ▸ Pause Recording
1049	/// (#98), directly under it with no key, pauses and resumes: retitled
1050	/// Resume Recording from the recorder's state, live only while a recording
1051	/// runs, and routed as the Stop is below — a second door beside the status
1052	/// item's rows (R2c), for a person who looks in the File menu first.
1053	///
1054	/// **Whose recording it is decides the route** (R1 review). The retitle reads
1055	/// the RECORDER, which is one object shared by the panel and the
1056	/// `record_screen` tool, so "Stop Recording" also shows over a recording the
1057	/// tool started — and the panel's `stopRecording()` rightly beeps at one that
1058	/// is not its own, which left the menu item a beep. So: the panel's own
1059	/// recording (its phase `.recording`, `.paused` or `.starting`) stops through
1060	/// the panel, which lands it exactly as its Stop button would; anything else
1061	/// the recorder holds stops through `ScreenRecorder.shared.stop()` with no
1062	/// completion, and the session's `onFinish` — the tool's — lands it; and
1063	/// with nothing recording the panel is shown. Pause Recording takes the
1064	/// same route: the panel's `.recording` / `.paused` through its own
1065	/// `pauseRecording()` / `resumeRecording()`, anything else through the
1066	/// recorder's `pause()` / `resume()`, whose refusal beeps.
1067	///
1068	/// **The welcome button has its own action** (R2 review). It used to send
1069	/// `newRecording`, whose first arm is the Stop above — but the button's
1070	/// title never changes, so a press during a recording stopped it under a
1071	/// label that said "New Recording…". `showRecorderPanel` only shows: during
1072	/// a recording that is a beep (`show()` while `hiddenForRecording`), which
1073	/// is what an un-retitled button can honestly do. The look and the title
1074	/// are untouched, since a chrome proof photographs the welcome window.
1075	extension AppDelegate {
1076	    @objc func newRecording(_ sender: Any?) {
1077	        let panel = RecorderPanelController.shared
1078	        switch panel.phase {
1079	        case .recording, .paused, .starting:
1080	            panel.stopRecording()
1081	        default:
1082	            if ScreenRecorder.shared.isRecording {
1083	                ScreenRecorder.shared.stop()
1084	            } else {
1085	                panel.show()
1086	            }
1087	        }
1088	    }

1090	    /// File ▸ Pause Recording / Resume Recording (the header). A tool's
1091	    /// status item flips at once, on the recorder's
1092	    /// `pauseDidChangeNotification` (#181).
1093	    @objc func pauseOrResumeRecording(_ sender: Any?) {
1094	        let panel = RecorderPanelController.shared
1095	        switch panel.phase {
1096	        case .recording:
1097	            panel.pauseRecording()
1098	        case .paused:
1099	            panel.resumeRecording()
1100	        default:
1101	            let recorder = ScreenRecorder.shared
1102	            do {
1103	                if recorder.isPaused { try recorder.resume() } else { try recorder.pause() }
1104	            } catch {
1105	                NSSound.beep()
1106	            }
1107	        }
1108	    }

423	enum CameraPreviewStep: Equatable {

425	    case message(String)
426	    case failed(String)

428	    case prepared
429	    case recording

433	/// The camera's live preview in the panel (camera-recording CR2b, spec §11
434	/// CAM-7) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s eleventh file, NEW rather than
435	/// cut, as `+Camera.swift` was: the rule that says what the well shows, and
436	/// the one sync that acts on it. The well is `CameraPreviewWell`, a grid row
437	/// of its own right under Format (`+Rows.swift`), shown only while a camera
438	/// is wanted: Source Camera, or "Record the camera too" beside a screen
439	/// source (spec §11 CAM-11 (4)).
440	///
441	/// **The step** (`cameraPreviewStep`, pure, first match wins): a panel not
442	/// visible or closing, or no camera wanted → off; a camera recording, or a
443	/// screen recording's camera beside it → its layer; the countdown or
444	/// starting → the prepared layer, never a build; any other phase, or a
445	/// busy recorder → blank; no camera → "No camera is connected."; the
446	/// Camera grant not authorized → a sentence; a prepared capture that
447	/// failed, or a build that threw → its sentence, never retried; else
448	/// prepare. The grant is read only at its own step, through
449	/// `grantDoors.cameraStatus`, so showing the panel never prompts and a
450	/// hidden panel reads nothing.
451	///
452	/// **The sync** runs at the end of `show()`, of every control change, of
453	/// `syncPhase()`, at the one-second tick while the panel is visible, and at
454	/// each device notification. Its first act applies a pending hot-plug
455	/// (`+Devices.swift`, CAM-8 (2)), so the step sees the new selection. It
456	/// keeps the row's visibility (refitting the window when it changes), lets
457	/// the prepared capture go when the well is off or shows a sentence while
458	/// everything is idle, stops a failed prepared capture once (not at every
459	/// tick, CAM-8 (6)), and otherwise hosts the layer the step names. The
460	/// capture is the recorder's (`ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`): the
461	/// countdown's `prepareCamera` keeps it, the panel's start adopts it, and a
462	/// tool's start never does (CAM-7 (7)), so through a tool's recording the
463	/// well reads "The camera is recording."
464	extension RecorderPanelController {
465	    static let previewGrantSentence = "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera."
466	    static let previewRecordingSentence = "The camera is recording."
467	
468	    /// CAM-7 (3)'s rule. `grant` and `failure` are called only at their own
469	    /// steps.
470	    static func cameraPreviewStep(
471	        visible: Bool, cameraSource: Bool, phase: Phase, recorderIdle: Bool,
472	        recordingCamera: Bool, cameraChosen: Bool, grant: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus,
473	        failure: () -> String?
474	    ) -> CameraPreviewStep {
475	        guard visible, cameraSource else { return .off }
476	        if recordingCamera { return .recording }
477	        switch phase {
478	        case .countdown, .starting: return .prepared
479	        case .idle: break
480	        case .recording, .paused, .stopping, .landing: return .blank
481	        }
482	        guard recorderIdle else { return .blank }
483	        guard cameraChosen else { return .message(CameraDevices.noCameraSentence) }
484	        guard grant() == .authorized else { return .message(Self.previewGrantSentence) }
485	        if let failure = failure() { return .failed(failure) }
486	        return .prepare
487	    }
488	
489	    /// The well's grid row.
490	    var cameraPreviewRow: NSGridRow? {
491	        (cameraPreview.superview as? NSGridView)?.cell(for: cameraPreview)?.row
492	    }
493	
494	    /// For the chosen camera at its resolved format (CAM-6 (3)): the
495	    /// prepared capture's stop on its own, else its failed start, else a
496	    /// failed build's record; nil when there is none.
497	    var previewFailure: String? {
498	        guard let id = selectedCameraID, let device = CameraDevices.device(withID: id) else {
499	            return nil
500	        }
501	        let facts = CameraDevices.facts(of: device)
502	        guard
503	            let format = CameraDevices.chosenFormat(
504	                selectedCameraFormat, in: facts.formats, active: facts.activeFormat)
505	        else { return nil }
506	        if let prepared = recorder.preparedCamera, prepared.deviceID == id, prepared.format == format,
507	            let sentence = prepared.stoppedOnItsOwn ?? prepared.startError?.localizedDescription
508	        {
509	            return sentence
510	        }
511	        guard let failure = recorder.preparedCameraFailure, failure.deviceID == id,
512	            failure.format == format
513	        else { return nil }
514	        return failure.sentence
515	    }

517	    /// A pending hot-plug applied (CAM-8 (2)), the row's visibility, then the
518	    /// step acted on (the type doc).
519	    func syncCameraPreview() {
520	        applyPendingDevices()
521	        let hidden = !cameraWanted
522	        if let row = cameraPreviewRow, row.isHidden != hidden {
523	            row.isHidden = hidden
524	            fitWindowToContent()
525	        }
526	        let step = Self.cameraPreviewStep(
527	            visible: window?.isVisible == true && !panelClosing, cameraSource: cameraWanted,
528	            phase: phase, recorderIdle: recorder.state == .idle,
529	            recordingCamera: recorder.cameraSession != nil || recorder.session?.cameraCapture != nil,
530	            cameraChosen: selectedCameraID != nil,
531	            grant: { Self.grantDoors.cameraStatus() }, failure: { self.previewFailure })
532	        switch step {
533	        case .off, .message:
534	            if phase == .idle, recorder.state == .idle { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
535	            if case .message(let sentence) = step {
536	                cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
537	            } else {
538	                cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
539	            }
540	        case .failed(let sentence):
541	            if let capture = recorder.preparedCamera?.capture, !capture.stopped { capture.stop() }
542	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
543	        case .prepare:
544	            recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
545	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
546	        case .prepared:
547	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
548	        case .recording:
549	            hostPreview(
550	                (recorder.cameraSession?.capture ?? recorder.session?.cameraCapture)?.previewLayer,
551	                else: Self.previewRecordingSentence)
552	        case .blank:
553	            cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
554	        }
555	    }

576	/// Hot-plug (camera-recording CR2c, spec §11 CAM-8) —
577	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s twelfth file, NEW rather than cut, as
578	/// `+Camera.swift` and `+CameraPreview.swift` were: the device observers,
579	/// the pending mark, the rebuild it applies, the selection rule and the
580	/// microphone list.
581	///
582	/// **The observers** are `AVCaptureDevice`'s connected and disconnected
583	/// notifications for any device, on main. `show()` adds the pair (one at
584	/// most) and adding it marks the lists pending, so a change made while the
585	/// panel was closed is caught up; `panelWillClose` removes them. A panel
586	/// ordered out for a recording keeps them.
587	///
588	/// **Pending until idle.** A notification marks the lists pending and steps
589	/// the preview (`syncCameraPreview`), whose FIRST act is
590	/// `applyPendingDevices`: it applies only while the panel's phase and the
591	/// recorder are both idle, so a change during a countdown, a recording or a
592	/// landing waits for the first step that finds both idle — the return to
593	/// idle draws the phase, which steps. It never steps the preview itself (no
594	/// recursion) and never persists.
595	///
596	/// **The rebuild** compares each popup's rows (id, title) with the devices
597	/// connected now and rebuilds only a popup that differs, so a menu the
598	/// person has open is not rebuilt for an unrelated device. The selection is
599	/// `hotPlugSelection` over the id held BEFORE the rebuild; the camera is
600	/// selected again — which rebuilds the Format popup, the stored format else
601	/// Best (CAM-6 (2)) — only when its popup was rebuilt or the id changed.
602	/// **No key is written**, so a camera that goes and comes back is selected
603	/// again with its stored format; the next control change writes what the
604	/// popups then show (CAM-5 (2)).

606	
607	    /// CAM-8 (3): `stored` when `listed` holds it, else `current` when
608	    /// listed, else nil (the default). `""` counts as nil for both.
609	    static func hotPlugSelection(listed: [String], stored: String?, current: String?) -> String? {
610	        let stored = stored.flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }
611	        let current = current.flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }
612	        if let stored, listed.contains(stored) { return stored }
613	        if let current, listed.contains(current) { return current }
614	        return nil
615	    }
616	
617	    /// The microphones connected now: the discovery session
618	    /// `ScreenRecorder.microphone(withID:)` asks, keeping only those whose
619	    /// `isConnected` is true (CAM-8 (5)).
620	    static func connectedMicrophones() -> [AVCaptureDevice] {
621	        AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession(
622	            deviceTypes: [.microphone, .external], mediaType: .audio, position: .unspecified
623	        ).devices.filter(\.isConnected)
624	    }
625	
626	    /// `popup`'s rows as a hot-plug compares them.
627	    static func hotPlugRows(of popup: NSPopUpButton) -> [HotPlugRow] {
628	        popup.itemArray.map { HotPlugRow(id: $0.representedObject as? String, title: $0.title) }
629	    }

633	    /// Idempotent: one pair at most. Adding the pair marks the lists
634	    /// pending, so the sync that follows catches up a change made while the
635	    /// panel was closed.
636	    func observeDevices() {
637	        guard deviceObservers.isEmpty else { return }
638	        let center = NotificationCenter.default
639	        let names = [AVCaptureDevice.wasConnectedNotification, AVCaptureDevice.wasDisconnectedNotification]
640	        for name in names {
641	            let observer = center.addObserver(forName: name, object: nil, queue: .main) {
642	                [weak self] _ in
643	                self?.devicesDidChange()
644	            }
645	            deviceObservers.append(observer)
646	        }
647	        devicesPending = true
648	    }

650	    /// Removes both observers.
651	    func stopObservingDevices() {
652	        deviceObservers.forEach(NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver)
653	        deviceObservers = []
654	    }

656	    /// A device came or went: the lists are pending, and the preview's step
657	    /// applies them first when the panel and the recorder are idle.
658	    func devicesDidChange() {
659	        devicesPending = true
660	        syncCameraPreview()
661	    }
662	
663	    // MARK: - The rebuild
664	
665	    /// CAM-8 (2)–(4): nothing unless pending and both idle; then each popup
666	    /// rebuilt only when its rows differ from the devices connected now, the
667	    /// selection `hotPlugSelection`'s, and the size note refreshed. Writes
668	    /// no key and never steps the preview.
669	    func applyPendingDevices() {
670	        guard devicesPending else { return }
671	        guard phase == .idle, recorder.state == .idle else { return }
672	        devicesPending = false
673	        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
674	
675	        let cameras = CameraDevices.connected()
676	        let cameraRows =
677	            cameras.isEmpty
678	            ? [HotPlugRow(id: nil, title: Self.noCameraTitle)]
679	            : cameras.map {
680	                HotPlugRow(id: $0.uniqueID, title: CameraDevices.popupTitle(CameraDevices.facts(of: $0)))
681	            }
682	        let currentCamera = selectedCameraID
683	        let cameraRebuilt = Self.hotPlugRows(of: cameraPopup) != cameraRows
684	        if cameraRebuilt { rebuildCameras() }
685	        let camera = Self.hotPlugSelection(
686	            listed: cameras.map(\.uniqueID), stored: defaults.string(forKey: Self.cameraKey),
687	            current: currentCamera)
688	        if cameraRebuilt || camera != selectedCameraID { selectCamera(camera) }

690	        let microphones = Self.connectedMicrophones()
691	        let microphoneRows =
692	            [HotPlugRow(id: nil, title: "Off")]
693	            + microphones.map { HotPlugRow(id: $0.uniqueID, title: $0.localizedName) }
694	        let currentMicrophone = microphonePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String
695	        if Self.hotPlugRows(of: microphonePopup) != microphoneRows { rebuildMicrophones() }
696	        selectMicrophone(

698	                listed: microphones.map(\.uniqueID),
699	                stored: defaults.string(forKey: Self.microphoneKey), current: currentMicrophone))

5	/// Everything the recorder panel does from Record pressed to the recording
6	/// RUNNING (road map 3, R1c) — the countdown, the start, the stop —
7	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s third file. The grants a press checks
8	/// first are `+Grants.swift`. The recording's END
9	/// and its landing are `+Landing.swift`, and the window picker is
10	/// `+Picker.swift`, both cut out along the lines `recordingEnded` and
11	/// `presentPicker` draw when the R1 review's fixes put this file past the
12	/// 400-line cap; the pause and the resume, and the phases drawn, are
13	/// `+Pause.swift` (R2c).
14	///
15	/// **Before the grants, the source** (R1 review): Record with the Source row
16	/// reading "Window…" and no picked filter refuses FIRST, by name, and starts
17	/// no countdown — `currentChoice()` would otherwise quietly fall back to the
18	/// main display and record the wrong thing. The picker is NOT presented from
19	/// the guard: a refusal that puts up a system UI is not a refusal. With
20	/// "Record the camera too" ticked (spec §11 CAM-11 (5)) no camera refuses
21	/// next, and the Camera grant is checked between Screen Recording and the
22	/// microphone; with it off the Camera grant is never read.
23	///
24	/// **The start is bounded and numbered** (R1 review). `.starting` used to
25	/// have no ceiling and no exit: `ScreenRecorder.shareableContent` can hold
26	/// its answer for tens of seconds on a locked console (measured ~37 s), and
27	/// a panel waiting on it showed "Starting…" with the button disabled and no
28	/// way back. Now each press of Record is one ATTEMPT with a number
29	/// (`startGeneration`), the lookup's completion carries the number and is
30	/// ignored once it is stale, and a one-shot timer at
31	/// `ScreenRecorder.armCeiling` fails the attempt with `.startTimedOut` while
32	/// the lookup is still pending. Once `launch` has handed the attempt to the
33	/// recorder its own arm ceiling is the bound (the same sentence, from the
34	/// start completion) and the panel's timer is cancelled, so the two cannot
35	/// both fire on one attempt.
36	///
37	/// **Stop while starting** (lane C's flag, closed by reading the seam):
38	/// after `launch` the recorder is arming and `stop()` is HELD — finishing
39	/// begins the moment the start lands, and the end arrives through the
40	/// session's `onFinish` like any other; a start that FAILS instead answers
41	/// the start completion alone, `onFinish` is never called for it, and
42	/// `startFailed` is the only thing that runs. Before `launch` there is
43	/// nothing to stop: `abandonStart` bumps the generation so the pending
44	/// answer is dropped, and the panel goes idle. Without that arm a Stop while
45	/// the lookup was pending left the panel at "Stopping…" for good, because
46	/// the answer then found the phase moved on and did nothing.
47	///
48	/// **The microphone is prepared at the countdown's start** (R1 review;
49	/// `ScreenRecorder+Microphone.swift` says why — `startRunning()`'s first-use
50	/// cost, up to 0.4 s of voice missing from the file) and discarded on cancel,
51	/// on close and on a refused start, so an input never stays open past the
52	/// recording it was for. **So is a camera's capture** (spec §11 CAM-5,

141	    /// 3, 2, 1 in the panel, one second each — `TimelineView.flashRefusal`'s
142	    /// shape: `[weak self]`, self-invalidating — added to the main run loop
143	    /// in `.common` modes (the type doc). The Record button reads Cancel
144	    /// meanwhile, and a click on it or closing the panel ends the countdown
145	    /// with nothing started. The microphone the choice names is prepared
146	    /// here, after the grants and before the first second has passed, so its
147	    /// start cost is paid while the numeral is still on screen — and the
148	    /// tick is armed at once, so the meter reads that session through the
149	    /// 3-2-1 (#98 c). A `resumeProblem` left by the last recording is cleared
150	    /// first, so its sentence does not carry into this one's note (#193).
151	    func beginCountdown() {
152	        countdownTimer?.invalidate()
153	        resumeProblem = nil
154	        phase = .countdown(Self.countdownSeconds)
155	        recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
156	        recorder.prepareMicrophone(currentChoice().microphone)
157	        armTick()
158	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
159	            guard let self, case .countdown(let remaining) = self.phase else {
160	                timer.invalidate()
161	                return
162	            }
163	            if remaining > 1 {
164	                self.phase = .countdown(remaining - 1)
165	            } else {
166	                timer.invalidate()
167	                self.countdownTimer = nil

169	            }
170	        }
171	        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
172	        countdownTimer = timer

185	    /// The choice as the controls stand, then the filter: a picked window's
186	    /// is the picker's own; a display's is built from the shareable content
187	    /// and leaves out what `recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows:)`
188	    /// names (`ScreenRecorder.filter(for:in:excluding:)`) — Frame Job's own
189	    /// application, which keeps the document windows out of a display
190	    /// recording's picture, or with Include Frame Job windows on the panel's
191	    /// window alone. One attempt, numbered and bounded (the type doc).
192	    private func startRecording() {
193	        let choice = currentChoice()
194	        let exclusion = recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows: choice.includeFrameJobWindows)
195	        startGeneration += 1
196	        let generation = startGeneration
197	        launched = false
198	        phase = .starting
199	        // A voice-over has no lookup to bound (`+VoiceOver.swift`).
200	        if choice.source == .voiceOver { return launchVoiceOver(choice) }
201	        // Nor does a camera: the recorder's own arm ceiling bounds it.
202	        if choice.source == .camera { return launchCamera(choice) }
203	        startTimer?.invalidate()
204	        startTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
205	            withTimeInterval: ScreenRecorder.armCeiling, repeats: false
206	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.armTimedOut(generation: generation) }
207	        if choice.source == .picked, let filter = pickedFilter {
208	            launch(filter: filter, choice: choice)
209	            return
210	        }
211	        ScreenRecorder.shareableContent { [weak self] outcome in
212	            guard let self, self.phase == .starting, generation == self.startGeneration else {
213	                return
214	            }
215	            switch outcome {
216	            case .failure(let error):
217	                self.startFailed(error)
218	            case .success(let content):
219	                do {
220	                    let filter = try ScreenRecorder.filter(
221	                        for: choice.source, in: content, excluding: exclusion)
222	                    self.launch(filter: filter, choice: choice)
223	                } catch {
224	                    self.startFailed(error)
225	                }
226	            }
227	        }
228	    }

230	    /// The arm ceiling, for the lookup half of an attempt: a stale number, a
231	    /// phase that moved on, or an attempt the recorder already holds (its
232	    /// own ceiling reports that one) does nothing. Internal so a probe can
233	    /// fire it without a lookup.

235	        guard phase == .starting, generation == startGeneration, !launched else { return }
236	        startFailed(RecorderError.startTimedOut)

240	    /// lookup's answer is orphaned by the generation bump, the prepared
241	    /// microphone let go, and the panel idle with a note saying nothing was
242	    /// recorded.
243	    private func abandonStart() {
244	        startGeneration += 1
245	        startTimer?.invalidate()
246	        startTimer = nil
247	        recorder.discardPreparedMicrophone()
248	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()
249	        phase = .idle
250	        setNote(Self.abandonedSentence)
251	    }

253	    private func launch(filter: SCContentFilter, choice: RecordingChoice) {
254	        // From here the recorder's arm ceiling is the bound.
255	        startTimer?.invalidate()
256	        startTimer = nil
257	        launched = true
258	        recorder.start(
259	            filter: filter, choice: choice, mayAsk: true,
260	            onFinish: { [weak self] outcome in self?.recordingEnded(outcome) }
261	        ) { [weak self] error in
262	            guard let self else { return }
263	            if let error {
264	                self.startFailed(error)
265	                return
266	            }
267	            self.recordingDidStart()
268	        }
269	    }

274	        startTimer?.invalidate()
275	        startTimer = nil
276	        launched = false
277	        recorder.discardPreparedMicrophone()
278	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()
279	        phase = .idle
280	        setNote(error.localizedDescription)

283	    /// The recording chrome (decision 7): the status item in the menu bar
284	    /// with Pause, Resume and Stop (`+Pause.swift` for the first two), the
285	    /// 30 Hz tick, and the panel ordered OUT for EVERY source until the
286	    /// landing has something to say — whether or not it was on screen

288	    /// `revealIfNoted` reads it). R1 hid it for a picked window only,
289	    /// because a display's filter excludes Frame Job (R0 q3); the user asked
290	    /// for the dialog to go away whatever is recorded, and the menu bar's
291	    /// item is the recording's controls now. A voice-over and a camera are
292	    /// the exceptions (`hidesForRecording`): the panel stays as it was, so it is never
293	    /// `hiddenForRecording` and `showWhenLanded` is simply whether it is up.
294	    func recordingDidStart() {
295	        // A stop asked for while arming has moved the phase on; the end
296	        // comes through `recordingEnded`.
297	        guard phase == .starting else { return }
298	        phase = .recording
299	        resumeProblem = nil
300	        setNote("")
301	        let item = RecorderStatusItem(
302	            keys: recorder.recordsKeys,
303	            onPause: { [weak self] in self?.pauseRecording() },
304	            onResume: { [weak self] in self?.resumeRecording() },
305	            onStop: { [weak self] in self?.stopRecording() })
306	        item.show()
307	        statusItem = item
308	        armTick()
309	        showWhenLanded = window?.isVisible == true
310	        guard Self.hidesForRecording(currentChoice().source) else { return }
311	        hiddenForRecording = true
312	        window?.orderOut(nil)

316	
317	    /// 30 Hz from the countdown's start, in `.common` modes (the type doc).
318	    /// Through `.countdown` and `.starting` it ONLY meters — the prepared
319	    /// session's level (#98 c; the recorder publishes nothing while
320	    /// arming, so the bar holds its last pre-roll level for that instant).
321	    /// While recording or paused: the microphone's level into the panel's
322	    /// own meter (`ScreenRecorder.publishMicrophoneLevel`, a no-op without
323	    /// a microphone and while paused, the recorder having silenced the
324	    /// bar), the elapsed time in the footnote and in the status item — with
325	    /// `paused`, which is what flips the item's menu — and a microphone
326	    /// problem into the note. `recordingDidStart` re-arms it.
327	    private func armTick() {
328	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
329	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1.0 / 30, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
330	            guard let self else {
331	                timer.invalidate()
332	                return
333	            }
334	            switch self.phase {
335	            case .countdown, .starting:
336	                self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
337	                return
338	            default:
339	                break
340	            }
341	            guard self.phase == .recording || self.phase == .paused || self.phase == .stopping
342	            else {
343	                timer.invalidate()
344	                return
345	            }
346	            self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
347	            self.refreshStatusLabel()
348	            self.statusItem?.update(elapsed: self.recorder.elapsed, paused: self.phase == .paused)
349	            self.syncMicrophoneNote()
350	        }
351	        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
352	        tickTimer = timer
353	    }

355	    /// The live note — what the panel says while a recording runs or is
356	    /// paused — rebuilt at every tick from its two PARTS and never from the
357	    /// label's text: `ScreenRecorder.microphoneProblem` the moment it is
358	    /// non-nil (a device unplugged, a writer that gave up), and
359	    /// `resumeProblem`, a resume the recorder refused (`+Pause.swift`,
360	    /// whose `liveNote` is the composition). Composing from the label was
361	    /// the R2 review's defect: a microphone did-finish landing late
362	    /// replaced a note that did not yet contain its sentence and wiped the
363	    /// resume's, and each retried resume appended its sentence again. Set
364	    /// only on a change, because `setNote` refits the window and this runs
365	    /// at 30 Hz.
366	    func syncMicrophoneNote() {
367	        let text = Self.liveNote(
368	            microphoneProblem: recorder.microphoneProblem, resumeProblem: resumeProblem)
369	        if noteLabel.stringValue != text { setNote(text) }
370	    }

372	    func disarmTick() {
373	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
374	        tickTimer = nil
375	    }
